title: Document-identity recovery model replacing the single recovery slot
outcome: Crash recovery is keyed by document identity: working in document B never destroys the recovery snapshot of document A, recovery restore preserves project identity, and the recovery picker (if any) only ever offers snapshots that still exist in the store.
before: GOVERNOR.md Active Risks (2026-08-27): single recovery slot with no per-document identity, acceptable for current local use but tracked; docs/reviews/sprint-critic-01.md P3: recovery-restore loses project identity, and deleting the open project re-creates it on next edit.
after: Per-document recovery records with identity-preserving restore, proven by tests that open two documents, dirty both, crash-simulate, and recover each independently.
acceptance: Two documents edited in sequence each retain an independent recoverable snapshot.
Recovery restore preserves project identity (name/id) rather than losing it.
Deleting a project does not resurrect it as a side effect of autosave.
Existing recovery and projects tests remain green.
npx tsc --noEmit, targeted tests, npm run test:chrome and npm run build pass.

builder.notes: Builder zcode-identity-pc2 (pc-cloud1), branch agent/viro-0011/zcode-gov-audit-pc1 based on main 50144659 (post-wave-merge). Inherited uncommitted prep drafts (src/app.ts, src/library/store.ts, tests/recovery-identity.*) from the banked prior seat; reviewed every line as incoming owner before adoption. Implementation: identity = project id via PressApp.ensureDocIdentity() (mints uid('proj') on first autosave when absent, shared by writeRecovery and persistCurrentProject so both sinks agree); RecoverySnapshot.id widened to string with optional createdAt — the recovery object store is already keyed by generic keyPath 'id', so NO DB version bump and no format migration; listRecovery() added (getAll + newest-first by savedAt); no-arg getRecovery() returns the newest record (legacy single-slot read semantics kept so tests/recovery.spec.mjs passes unmodified); restoreRecovery(id?) adopts currentProjectId only for proj_-prefixed ids (legacy 'current' restores under a freshly minted id, never adopting the slot key) and resumes the record's createdAt; deleteProject(id) also deleteRecovery(id) so a deleted document can never resurrect through recovery and its identity is never reused; discardAllRecoveries() added for diagnostics/clean-slate; pendingRecovery stays the newest-first head of pendingRecoveries so the existing recover bar (src/chrome/desk.ts reads only pendingRecovery + no-arg restore/discard) works with ZERO chrome changes. Before-state proof: draft unit tests run RED 0/5 on unmodified main (stash of src changes), GREEN 5/5 after. Honest records: package.json test:unit list and tests/slices.mjs SCRIPTS are OUTSIDE the granted lease (tests/recovery-identity-* only), so the new suites are run by documented command rather than wired into npm scripts; wiring them in is left to the Governor/Verifier coordination.

critic.notes: Persistence behavior only; no visual redesign.
